input: Set up automatic bill payments online

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The number and types of bills (utilities, subscriptions, loans, credit cards, etc.) determine how many accounts need to be set up and whether a single platform can handle all of them.
Knowing whether this is for a household, a business, or a single individual affects account ownership, shared access, and how payments should be organized.
Whether the user is starting from scratch or already has some bills set up partially determines where in the process to begin.
The payment source — bank account (ACH), credit card, or a bill-pay service — shapes which setup steps are needed and what fees or rewards may apply.
A hard deadline (e.g., a bill due soon) or a tight window for setup changes the priority order of which bills to automate first.
Some users want full autopay (full balance paid automatically), others prefer a fixed minimum or a custom amount — this directly affects how each autopay rule is configured.
Knowing whether the user wants confirmation alerts, a spending overview, or simply zero missed payments defines what a fully successful setup looks like.

gold.taskTitle: Set up automatic bill payments online
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to configure automatic online payments for their bills so that payments are made without manual intervention each cycle.

questions.title: Which specific bills do you want to automate?
questions.description: Identify the exact bill types — such as utilities, credit cards, rent, streaming services, or loans — that should be included in the autopay setup.

questions.title: Is this for personal use or a shared household or business?
questions.description: Clarify who owns and accesses the accounts to determine if shared logins, joint accounts, or business banking considerations apply.

questions.title: Have you set up any automatic payments before?
questions.description: Determine whether the user is starting from scratch or building on an existing partial setup, so the plan starts at the right step.

questions.title: Do you want payments drawn from a bank account or a credit card?
questions.description: Establish the preferred funding source — ACH bank transfer, credit card, or a third-party bill-pay service — since each has different enrollment steps.

questions.title: Is any bill due soon and needs to be set up urgently?
questions.description: Identify any hard deadlines so the most time-sensitive bills are prioritized at the start of the plan.

questions.title: Should autopay cover the full balance or a fixed amount?
questions.description: Determine the payment rule preference — full statement balance, minimum due, or a custom fixed amount — especially relevant for credit cards and variable bills.

questions.title: Do you want alerts or a tracker after payments go out?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user wants email or SMS payment confirmations, a spending dashboard, or simply a set-and-forget arrangement with no extra notifications.
